q: What is the minimum number of people a passenger car must carry to use an HOV lane on a provincial highway?
e: HOV = at least 2 people (buses, taxis, green-plate cars and some others are exempt).
s: vehicles carrying at least two people

q: On a freeway, how far ahead should you look?
a: About 15 to 20 seconds ahead (or as far as you can see)
w: About 2 seconds ahead
About 5 seconds ahead
Only at the car in front
e: At higher speeds you need to look farther ahead.
s: Look ahead to where you are going to be in the next 15 to 20 seconds, or as far ahead as you can see, when you travel at faster speeds.

q: You're driving in the right lane of a freeway. A car is coming up the on-ramp to merge. What should you do?
a: If it's safe, move over a lane to leave room for the merging car
w: Speed up so it has to merge behind you
Stop to let it in
Honk to warn it
e: Freeway drivers should move over, if it's safe, to leave room for merging vehicles.
s: Freeway drivers should move over, if it is safe to do so, leaving room for merging vehicles.

q: You're in the acceleration lane of a freeway entrance. What's your job?
a: Signal, speed up to match freeway traffic, and merge smoothly into a safe gap
w: Stop at the end of the lane and wait
Merge slowly and let freeway traffic adjust to you
Drive on the shoulder until there's a gap
e: The acceleration lane is for matching the speed of the traffic you're joining.
s: Signal and increase your speed to merge smoothly with traffic.

q: On a freeway, is it OK for a slower vehicle to change lanes in front of a faster one?
a: No: it's dangerous and illegal for a slower vehicle to cut in front of a faster vehicle
w: Yes, if it signals first
Yes, slower vehicles have the right-of-way
Only if the faster vehicle is speeding
e: Be careful not to cut off any vehicle when changing lanes or joining traffic.
s: It is dangerous and illegal for a slower moving vehicle to cut in front of a faster moving vehicle.

q: You're in the far LEFT lane of a divided highway with three lanes your way. An ambulance comes up behind you with its siren on. Where should you pull over?
a: To the nearest edge of the road, which here is the left side
w: Across all lanes to the right shoulder
Stop right where you are
Onto the left shoulder and keep driving
e: On a one-way road or divided highway with more than two lanes, move to the closest curb or edge.
s: When on a one-way road or divided highway having more than two lanes of traffic, move to the closest curb or edge of the roadway.

q: Some freeway entrance ramps join on the LEFT. What does that mean for you?
a: You enter the fastest lane first, so you must match your speed more quickly
w: You have the right-of-way over freeway traffic
You should stop at the end of the ramp
You must cross to the right lane right away
e: Use the acceleration lane to match your speed to the traffic.
s: A few entrance ramps join the freeway on the left. This means you enter the fastest lane of traffic first.

q: Traffic on the freeway is jammed. Why must you keep off the shoulder?
a: Emergency vehicles use the shoulder when all lanes are blocked
w: The shoulder is only for trucks
The shoulder is a passing lane in traffic jams
It's fine to use the shoulder in a jam
e: Don't drive on or block the shoulder on freeways.
s: Don't drive on or block the shoulder on freeways. Emergency vehicles will use the shoulder of the road if all lanes are blocked.

q: When leaving a freeway, when should you start slowing down?
a: Once you're in the deceleration lane
w: While still in the freeway lane, before signalling
Only at the end of the exit ramp
As soon as you see the exit sign
e: Signal and move into the deceleration lane first. Don't slow down on the freeway itself.
s: When leaving the freeway, signal that you want to move into the deceleration lane, but do not slow down.

q: You missed your freeway exit. What must you NOT do?
a: Stop or back up on the freeway
w: Take the next exit
Keep driving at a steady speed
Check your mirrors
e: Never stop or reverse on a freeway. Just take the next exit.
s: If you miss an exit, do not stop or reverse on the freeway. Take the next exit.

q: A large truck has three people in it. May it use the HOV lane?
a: No: large trucks are never allowed in HOV lanes, no matter how many people are inside
w: Yes, with 2 or more people
Yes, outside rush hour
Only if it's under 10 tonnes
e: Large trucks are not permitted in HOV lanes.
s: Large trucks are not permitted on the HOV lanes, regardless of the number of occupants.

q: Which of these may use a provincial HOV lane with only the driver inside?
a: A car with green licence plates
w: A regular car
A large truck
A pickup truck
e: Green-plate (plug-in hybrid and electric) vehicles may use HOV lanes with any number of people. So may licensed taxis and airport limousines.
s: Vehicles with the “Green” licence plate are permitted in the HOV lane with any number of occupants.

q: Once you've merged onto the freeway, where should you normally drive?
a: In the right-hand lane, using the left lanes only for passing
w: In the far left lane, since it's fastest
In whichever lane is emptiest
In the centre lane, always
e: Keep right; pass on the left; don't stay in the left lane.
s: Traffic should keep to the right, using the left lanes for passing.

q: You've just left a freeway onto the exit ramp. Why should you check your speedometer?
a: After driving fast, you may be going faster than you think ("velocitization")
w: To check your fuel use
Because ramps have no speed limits
To see if you can speed up
e: Speed adaptation makes slow speeds feel slower than they are.
s: Losing your ability to judge your speed accurately is sometimes called speed adaptation or velocitization.

q: Your car starts having trouble on the freeway. What should you do?
a: Pull over to the nearest shoulder right away, with your hazard lights on
w: Keep going until it stalls
Stop in your lane and turn on hazards
Slow down in the left lane
e: At the first sign of trouble, pull over. Never stop in the driving lanes.
s: At the first sign of trouble, begin to pull over. Do not wait for your vehicle to stall on the freeway.

q: You're stopped on the freeway shoulder waiting for help. What should you do?
a: Stay in your car with the doors locked
w: Stand behind your car to wave down help
Raise the hood and walk to the nearest exit
Sit on the guardrail
e: Don't raise the hood. If someone stops, ask them to call police for you.
s: While you wait for help, stay in your vehicle with the doors locked.

q: You must get out of your broken-down car on the freeway shoulder. Which door should you use?
a: The door away from traffic, if possible
w: The driver's door, always
Whichever door is fastest
Climb out a window
e: Be careful getting out, and leave through the door away from traffic if you can.
s: If possible, leave through the door away from traffic.

q: How should you drive near large trucks on a freeway?
a: Stay clear of them and leave space around your car
w: Follow closely to save fuel
Drive beside them for a long time
Cut in front of them after passing
e: Large vehicles block your view. Space gives you time to react.
s: Stay clear of large vehicles. Because of their size, they block your view more than other vehicles.

q: Exit signs on a freeway are posted far in advance. Why?
a: So you have time to make any lane changes safely
w: So you can slow down on the freeway
So you can stop and read them
They are for trucks only
e: Plan your lane change early.
s: Signs telling you that there are freeway exits ahead are far enough in advance for you to make any lane changes safely.

q: When may a G1 driver drive on a freeway?
a: Only with a licensed driving instructor
w: Any time, with any accompanying driver
Only during the day
Only on weekends
e: New drivers should learn to drive at low speeds first.
s: Class G1 drivers may only drive on freeways with a licensed driving instructor.

q: What separates an HOV lane from the other lanes, and what is the rule?
a: A striped buffer zone, and it's illegal to cross it
w: A solid yellow line that you may cross any time
Orange cones you may drive between
Nothing; you may enter anywhere
e: Enter and leave HOV lanes only at the marked entry/exit zones.
s: The HOV lane is separated from the other general traffic lanes by a striped buffer zone. It is illegal and unsafe to cross the striped buffer pavement markings.

q: When are provincial HOV lanes in effect?
a: 24 hours a day, 7 days a week
w: Only during rush hour
Only on weekdays
Only in winter
e: Provincial HOV lanes are open 24/7.
s: HOV lanes are open 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

q: A police officer stops you for using an HOV lane improperly. Besides a ticket, what must you do?
a: Return to the general lanes at the next entry/exit zone
w: Pull onto the shoulder and wait
Pay the fine on the spot
Nothing else
e: Improper HOV use is also 3 demerit points.
s: You will be required to re-enter the general lanes at the next entry/exit zone.

q: What must a commercial vehicle have to use an HOV lane?
a: Two or more people, and be under 6.5 metres long
w: A green plate
Only a valid permit
One person, if it's a delivery
e: Large trucks are never allowed, but smaller commercial vehicles can qualify.
s: Commercial motor vehicles must have two or more people in the vehicle and be less than 6.5 metres in total length to be in the HOV lane.
